tier_reason: Tier C stands, but the enricher's reading of the harness invalidates the headline 10-bit rows: tools/bench passes element counts as strides (yPlaneStride = inWidth on uint16 planes) while YCbCrP16-inl.h takes bytes, so sparkyuv reads overlapping half-size planes against libyuv's full planes, on top of the different output depth already noted. The unpremultiply 1.54x is NEON against libyuv's C fallback (ARGBUnattenuate has no NEON version). Valid like-for-like rows are the 8-bit decodes: 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 1.32x, 4:4:4 1.10x, NV12/NV21 ties; libyuv wins the encodes. A correctness bug sits in src/YCbCr420-inl.h (the 8-bit 4:2:0 SIMD encoder reloads mSrc instead of the next row, so vertical chroma averaging is a no-op and disagrees with the scalar tail); it is on the encode rows, which libyuv already wins.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Valid like-for-like rows (README, Apple M3 Pro, ns per call, derived from page data): 8-bit decode 4:2:2 346,422 vs libyuv 458,754 (1.32x); 4:2:0 347,903 vs 458,823 (1.32x); 4:4:4 332,122 vs 365,939 (1.10x); NV21 and NV12 tie. Invalid rows: the 10-bit decodes (1.92-2.12x) pass element counts as byte strides so sparkyuv reads half-size planes and writes a different output depth; unpremultiply 1.54x is NEON vs libyuv's C fallback. Slower than libyuv: RGBA8 to YCbCr420 (libyuv 2.0x faster), RGBA8 to YCbCr422 (1.37x), premultiply (1.21x).
corrections.caveats: Headline 10-bit wins are a harness bug (element counts passed as byte strides) and compare different output depths; the valid wins are 8-bit decodes at 1.10-1.32x on NEON only. No tests (CI runs ctest with none defined), no libyuv equality check; the NV12 and NV21 libyuv calls are swapped, the libyuv 4:2:2 decode is fed 4:2:0 chroma, and J422 full range is compared against TV range. The 8-bit 4:2:0 SIMD encoder has a vertical chroma averaging bug (src/YCbCr420-inl.h). Depends on the author's Highway fork (awxkee/highway, widen_mul). libyuv is a prebuilt libyuv.a of unknown version and flags; arm64 numbers only; repo archived by its owner.

tier_reason: Tier C stands. Enricher corrections: the README tables date from November 2024 to January 2025 (git blame) with yuv-sys 0.3.7, which is libyuv 1886. The Windows column is invalid: cc builds libyuv with cl.exe, and libyuv 1886 on x64 MSVC has only the I422/I444ToARGBRow_SSSE3 paths, every other row running C, which explains the 2.70-6.86 ms libyuv times. The NEON 10-bit 2x is SIMD against C (no I210ToARGBRow_NEON in 1886). The RGB to YUV 4:2:0 benches behind the 1.20x NEON encode figure are commented out at HEAD (app/benches/yuv8/main.rs lines 128-344). Valid like-for-like wins are the 8-bit NEON and Linux x86 rows at 1.07-1.95x.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Valid like-for-like rows (README, derived from page data; libyuv 1886 via yuv-sys 0.3.7, tables from Nov 2024 to Jan 2025): NV12 to RGBA 377.59 vs 621.11 us on NEON (1.64x), 917.52 vs 979.96 us on AVX2 (1.07x), 736.21 vs 800.85 us on AVX-512 (1.09x); YUV 4:2:0 to RGB 346.13 vs 675.72 us NEON (1.95x), 923.83 us vs 1.42 ms AVX2 (1.54x), 614.19 us vs 1.16 ms AVX-512 (1.89x); YUV 4:2:0 to RGBA 396.58 vs 710.88 us NEON (1.79x), 942.92 us vs 1.03 ms AVX2 (1.09x), 733.88 vs 870.64 us AVX-512 (1.19x). The RGB to YUV 4:2:0 encode rows (1.13-1.35x) come from benches commented out at HEAD; the Windows column and the NEON 10-bit rows compare SIMD against libyuv C fallbacks and are not valid.
corrections.caveats: Windows column invalid (cl.exe-built libyuv 1886 has SSSE3 only for I422/I444ToARGB; other rows run C); NEON 10-bit 2x is SIMD against C. No output comparison against libyuv; open issue #144 (SIMD and scalar paths differ by 2); the fuzz crate skips the sse and avx paths; toolchain is an undated nightly. libyuv wins several AVX2 and AVX-512 rows (4:0:0, 4:4:4 and 4:2:2 to RGBA; RGBA to YUV 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 on AVX-512; 10-bit to RGBA8 on AVX2).
